Name: AraHeritage
Description: A large-scale Arabic Facebook corpus of historical and cultural heritage discourse.
Paper Title: AraHeritage: Exploring Historical and Cultural Heritage Discourse on Arabic Facebook
Abstract: We introduce AraHeritage, a large-scale Arabic-dominant Facebook corpus of historical and cultural heritage discourse comprising 290,390 public posts collected between June 22 and August 7, 2024. The corpus was constructed through hashtag-based collection using five heritage-oriented seed terms: خيﺭات (history), ﺙﺍرت (heritage), يخيﺭات (historical), ميدق (ancient/old), and يضاملﺍ (the past). Analysis reveals that Arabic heritage discourse on Facebook is not a monothematic domain but a hybrid communicative space in which historical and cultural content coexists with sports-driven engagement, tourism references, and political commentary. Photo posts dominate total interaction by volume, while Native Video records the highest mean engagement among the major formats and link-based posts underperform. Engagement is geographically concentrated, with Egypt and Algeria accounting for the largest single-country shares. The corpus provides a high-resolution snapshot of Arabic digital heritage communication and supports research in related studies.
